about: Controls that change nothing to see when operated alone, by design. controls.mjs reports each under 'Could not tell' with its reason, so none is hidden and none counts as dead. A label matches when it starts with `control`; `backend` limits a row to webgpu or webgl2. `reason` is for a control that changes nothing; `stops` is for stops of a slider or select that draw the same picture by design (a value the picture does not show). Add a row only with the next action that shows the control working.

controls.reason: it sets how the next strike ends (held lit until Return to night); press Trigger a strike to see it
a cast selects its first contact and moves the probe there; this cast found one contact, so clicking it again keeps the probe where it is (with more contacts, choosing another moves it)
it sets how the camera moves at the next shot change (a cut instead of a glide); pick another shot to see it
the exhibit's three methods (weighted, moment, exact) are all order-independent transparency, and this control shows it: the picture stays the same when the draw order is reversed
the wall culls the statue's clusters only while the wall slider puts it in front of the statue; at the starting position it hides nothing, so the drawn count stays the same

controls.stops: the rating is an IFC property value with no geometry: any value other than the file's marks the door's frame amber as an edit queued for export, so 24, 36 and 48 dB draw the same frame; the readout shows the value and Prepare file writes it
0 and 30 input turns draw the same drive: the flexspline turns back exactly once in 30 input turns (ratio -1/30), so every part is where it started; the turn readout tells them apart
it chooses the axis the range form edits; press Apply range to select rows on that axis
it fills the range form; press Apply range to select rows (a value outside the axis gets a message instead)

fog hides what lies behind it as exp(-density times distance), so by 40 percent the far trees are mostly hidden and 50 adds little to see (at most 8 of 255); 0 and 100 differ by up to 92 of 255
